subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (FintechX)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (FintechX)

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand FintechX's production plans. Below is a short recap + a few clarifying questions so we can size a Dedicated pool that meets your latency and cost goals.

Recap (from our discussion)
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated capacity (data isolation + predictable throughput). You also want the option to fall back to Hosted for burst traffic.
- Workload: multi-turn assistant + batch document summarization. Primary model family: open Llama-style model tuned for finance.
- SLO: 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for typical requests; burst handling for peak events.

Sizing questions / asks (can you confirm asap?):
1) TPS targets: you mentioned ~50 sustained TPS for conversational traffic and spikes up to ~150 TPS during peak trading windows — please confirm sustained vs peak windows (minutes/hours).
2) Concurrency: is the 12 concurrent inference requests number per region or global? Any differences across EU/US?
3) Token mix: rough breakdown of request sizes (input & output). Example: what fraction are short queries (<512 tokens), medium (512–2048), long (>2048)? Also typical input vs generated output token counts.
4) Model & precision: do you want us to size for H100-class performance (fp16 / int8-friendly) or plan to start on A100-class GPUs?
5) Batch & KV cache expectations: will you be reusing contexts heavily (long-running chat sessions) or mostly stateless single-turn calls?

Attached is a quick capacity_estimate.xlsx with a baseline worksheet (assumptions we used). I'll iterate once I get your answers. If it's easier, we can hop on a 30-min sync next week to finalize.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Elena Garcia <elena@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechx.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (FintechX)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Answers inline below.

1) TPS targets: confirmed — target steady-state is ~50 TPS for the conversational API during market hours (US market hours). Spikes: up to ~150 TPS for short bursts lasting ~5–30 minutes during large event windows (earnings, market opens). We also have nightly batch jobs that can run for longer periods but are lower priority.

2) Concurrency: the 12 concurrent requests number is per-region (we operate primarily in us-east-1) — early EU traffic is low and can be handled by Hosted.

3) Token mix: rough breakdown for the conversational assistant: ~70% short (<512 tokens, avg input 120 tokens / output 80 tokens), ~20% medium (512–2048 tokens, avg input 900 / output 400), ~10% long (>2048 tokens, long-form summarization; avg input 2400 / output 600). The nightly batch summarization jobs have higher long-token ratios but can be scheduled into off-peak capacity.

4) Model & precision: we prefer H100-class performance if the price delta makes sense — engineer preference for H100 due to sequence-length and throughput characteristics. If H100 not available initially, A100 is acceptable with a plan to migrate.

5) Cache expectations: conversational sessions reuse KV cache heavily (users have multi-turn sessions and we expect 3–8k token histories for a small percentage of sessions). Batch jobs are stateless.

Attached our procurement contact for contract steps. Happy to jump on a call if helpful — cc'd procurement.

Best,
Elena Garcia
Director, AI Platforms
FintechX
elena@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, procurement@fintechx.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up (FintechX)

Appreciate the quick answers — very helpful. Based on your inputs I've sketched a recommended Dedicated configuration and a short rationale below. See updated sheet in capacity_estimate.xlsx (tab: "FintechX - recommended").

High-level recommendation (US region):
- Baseline pool: 3 x H100 nodes (reserved)
  - Rationale: supports ~45–60 sustained TPS for your 70% short / 20% mid request mix with KV cache reuse; gives headroom for concurrency=12 and typical token mixes.
- Burst autoscaling: allow up to +3 H100s (total 6) for short spikes to ~150 TPS (autoscale policy with 5–10 minute cool-down).
- Fallback routing: configure automatic fallback to Hosted endpoints for non-critical batch jobs and for excess burst above the dedicated autoscale cap.
- Config notes: enable KV prefix caching for chat sessions (significant cost/latency savings for reused contexts); enable int8 pathways where model supports it to reduce capacity needs.

If you want a lower-cost starting point, an alternate config is 4 x A100 nodes with the same autoscaling headroom; this will increase latency slightly on long-context requests but may reduce committed spend. Given your preference for H100, I recommend reserving H100s for peak-critical months (earnings season) and starting with a mixed approach otherwise.

Next steps:
- If this looks reasonable, I’ll draft a Statement of Work + pricing (SOW-draft.pdf attached) and loop legal/procurement.
- Suggested follow-up call: Thu 18 Jun 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri 19 Jun 09:00–09:30 PT — I can include Rafael (solutions infra) to confirm autoscale tuning.

Two quick notes on assumptions we used (also in the sheet):
- Avg generation length for medium requests assumed 400 output tokens.
- KV cache reuse reduces compute by ~25% on sessions where history is reused (we accounted for this).

Would you prefer I size the pool more conservatively (e.g., 2x H100 baseline + more aggressive autoscale) or more aggressively (4x H100 baseline)?

Thanks,
Marissa
